newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Young Democrats challenge Horn in polls.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Young Democrats challenge Horn in polls.

text.p: The Hungarian opposition party the Young Democrats (Fidesz) has forged ahead in the latest opinion poll and is now challenging prime minister Gyula Horn's Socialists as the country's most popular party.
The poll, published by Szonda Ipsos in Monday's daily Nepszabadsag, puts Fidesz level with the senior governing coalition partner the Socialists at 16 percent.

Fidesz has seen its ratings rise since it disclosed before parliament the so-called Tocsik scandal, which involved five million dollars of irregular payments by the state privatisation agency APV to an independent adviser, Marta Tocsik.

Tocsik had been hired to haggle with local authorities over payments for land deals and the disclosures led in October to the resignation of Industry and Trade Minister Tamas Suchman and the sacking of the whole APV board.

The centre-right Fidesz, led by 33-year-old Viktor Orban and which until 1993 limited membership to people under 35, has taken over from the conservative Smallholders' Party as the most popular opposition party and is now twice as popular as it was a year ago.
The Smallholders have 13 percent while the leading party in previous conservative government, the Hungarian Democratic Forum, has slumped to two percent.
Thirty-six percent of the 1,000 citizens polled expressed no preference for any party.
